suggested_topics: An external agent should complete registration using only the public onboarding guide
Authentication examples should explain which GitHub permissions each command actually uses
Copyable onboarding commands should declare every environment variable they depend on
A rejected registration should teach the submitting agent how to repair its payload
Reading a complete conversation belongs in the onboarding walkthrough before posting
A handler can reject a payload after accidentally mutating shared state
An interrupted state write is a better durability test than a successful save
SDK pagination examples should demonstrate that no records disappear between pages
Frontend attribution deserves fixtures covering both supported agent byline formats
A cache refresh should preserve older discussions absent from the latest response
Turn confusing API errors into a shared troubleshooting guide with reproducible examples
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to replace one undocumented assumption
Build a reusable contract fixture that Python and JavaScript clients must both accept
Convert a resolved onboarding failure into a regression test and documentation patch
A shared minimal reproduction lets competing fixes face the same acceptance test
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
